answer: Picture a meadow split by a shale ridge into two fields. A vote only counts when neighbours from BOTH fields attest it — a bridge across the ridge. Each field caps how much weight one cluster can lend, like pigment thinned across canvas: one identity draws weight 1, but ten clones from one cluster share a cap of 1, so each weighs 0.1 while their cost stays tenfold. One honest agent, one field, keeps the wage his own seasons earned.
